Overview

About Natural Stone

ERA natural stone comes in a wide range of varieties, each cut and finished for walls, floors and landscapes. Because every slab is formed by nature, the veining, grain and colour change from piece to piece, which gives your space a finish no printed material can copy.

Natural stone for cladding and flooring that brings depth and character to every wall and floor. Each slab carries its own pattern, so no two spaces look alike.

Types & quality

Choose the right Natural Stone

Swatches are digital renderings that show the look of each type. The real product's colour and finish can vary a little.

Indoor floors

Marble

A metamorphic stone formed from limestone, known for flowing veins and a polished shine. Softer than granite, so it needs sealing and gentle cleaners.

Best for: Indoor floors, feature walls, vanities

Outdoor floors

Granite

An igneous stone made of quartz, feldspar and mica crystals, which gives the speckled look. Very hard and resistant to scratches, heat and weather.

Best for: Outdoor floors, steps, kitchen counters

Wall cladding

Sandstone

Formed from compressed sand grains, with warm earthy tones and a natural grip. It is porous, so sealing helps outdoors.

Best for: Wall cladding, garden paving, sit-outs

Interior floors

Limestone

A calcium-rich sedimentary stone with a soft, even, pale colour and fine pits. It suits calm interiors but reacts to acids.

Best for: Interior floors, wall panels, fireplaces

Bathrooms

Slate

A fine-grained metamorphic stone that splits into thin layers. Dark tones, a naturally rough surface, and strong against water and slips.

Best for: Bathrooms, patios, wall cladding

Kitchen tops

Quartzite

Sandstone transformed by heat and pressure into very hard, dense stone with a light crystal-like shimmer. Low water absorption.

Best for: Kitchen tops, outdoor floors, facades

Pool surrounds

Travertine

A sedimentary stone from mineral springs, with natural bands and small pits. Stays cooler underfoot; pits come filled or unfilled.

Best for: Pool surrounds, terraces, bathrooms

Feature walls

Stone cladding

Thin split-stone pieces stacked in rows (ledgestone) to give a rough, layered 3D wall. Lighter than full stone blocks.

Best for: Feature walls, exteriors, fireplaces

Made from & benefits

What Natural Stone is made of

Natural stone forms over millions of years from minerals in the earth. It is cut from quarries and finished, but never changed into another material.

Natural rockMarbleGraniteSandstoneLimestoneSlateQuartziteTravertine

08

Material guide

Know your material

What it is

Natural stone is quarried rock cut into slabs, tiles or panels. Each type has its own hardness, porosity and look.

How it is made

Blocks are cut at the quarry, then sawn, calibrated and finished (polished, honed, flamed or brushed) in the factory.

Installation tip

Fix with suitable adhesive on a level, dry base. Use movement joints on large outdoor areas.

Strengths

  • Long life when installed and sealed properly
  • Every piece is unique
  • Stays cool underfoot in hot weather

Good to know

  • Heavy, so it needs a strong base
  • Marble and limestone can stain or etch without sealing
09

FAQ

Common questions

Which stone is best for outdoors?

Granite, sandstone, slate and quartzite usually cope best with weather and wear. Choose a textured or flamed finish for grip.

Does stone need sealing?

Porous stones such as marble, limestone and travertine should be sealed. Granite and quartzite need less.

10

Care & maintenance

Easy to look after

  1. 01

    Seal the surface after installation, especially marble, limestone and travertine.

  2. 02

    Clean with a pH-neutral cleaner and avoid acids.

  3. 03

    Wipe spills quickly to prevent stains.
